newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF to change sugar contract quality, add ports.
newsitem.headline: MATIF to change sugar contract quality, add ports.

text.p: French futures and options exchange MATIF is changing two key specifications on its white sugar futures contract -- starting with the October 1998 trading month, exchange holding company Matif SA said.
The changes, to come into force when October 1998 starts trading on April 16, follow consultation with the industry and have been cleared by Paris regulators, it said in a statement.
-- In the first change, Matif SA said sugar quoted from October 1998, and from then onwards, would be reflect a colour value of 45 Icumsa instead of 60 Icumsa traded at present.
-- The second change involves adding two new ports where the sugar can be delivered when contracts expire. They are Durban in South Africa and Puerto Quetzal in Guatemala.
"Operators will benefit through this from access to production zones that have seen increases in exports in recent years," the French exchange said.
Matif SA said the COB financial watchdog in Paris had not exercised its right to veto the changes.
The changes in Paris sugar trading come hard on the heels of revisions to the No.5 white sugar contract traded on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange.
LIFFE said on Friday it was reducing the maximum Icumsa colour for non-EU ports for delivery against the contract to 45 units from 60, starting with the August 1998 delivery contract.
The British exchange also increased the minimum loading rate for sugars delivered in fulfilment of delivery obligations to 1,000 tonnes a day from 750 tonnes.
LIFFE chief executive Daniel Hodson said the aim was to ensure contract specifications remained "closely in line with current commercial practice in the underlying sugar market."

In the latest monthly volume figures for MATIF, the exchange's dollar-denominated white sugar contract traded a combined 11,942 lots in March, down 24.3 percent from the previous month, and down 34.3 percent from March 1996.
At the end of last month, the same contact had total open interest of 8,975 lots.
